objective: Compare external agent-memory configurations by measuring whether they preserve current S3 invariants across isolated coding tasks, stale-memory conflicts, session boundaries, and cross-agent handoffs.

configurations.description: No durable memory between task phases; only the current prompt and repository are available.
The agent may use the active model context but no external durable memory service.
AI-MEMORY is the external durable memory provider under test.
AI-MEMORY is used with an S3 correctness/integrity validation layer before durable conclusions are trusted.

protocol.result_collection: Run every scenario in an isolated clean worktree, persist one scenario result JSON, then aggregate one provider configuration at a time.
rules: Pin the same S3 commit for every provider configuration in a comparison.
Use the same agent model, harness version, task text, and tool permissions across provider configurations unless the scenario explicitly requires a distinct receiving agent.
Do not reuse modified worktrees, unrecorded notes, transcripts, or hidden handoff files between scenarios.
For cross-session scenarios, end Session A and start Session B without the Session A transcript; only the configured durable memory channel may carry state.
For cross-agent scenarios, Agent B must have a distinct agent or harness identity and must not receive Agent A's transcript.
For stale-memory scenarios, inject the declared stale claim unchanged and allow the agent to reconcile it against current repository evidence.
Invariant recall is informative. Correctness oracle failures always dominate recall scores.
Do not persist credentials, tokens, private host metadata, personal paths, environment dumps, or network identifiers in observations/results.

scenarios.purpose: Baseline retention of an explicit host-process safety policy during an ordinary repository change.
Retain the distinction between balanced subtraction and machine numeric difference across a later compiler session.
Retain checked i64 overflow and division-failure semantics across later numeric refactoring.
Prevent a later optimization session from importing an invalid machine noalias assumption from source &mut.
Reject an obsolete durable claim when current repository evidence says otherwise.
Carry multiple invariants through a clean session boundary with no transcript reuse.
Carry multiple invariants between distinct coding-agent identities using shared durable memory.
